newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: World oils/fats market seen growing in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: World oils/fats market seen growing in 1996/97.

text.p: Rising consumption is expected to boost the market for edible and soap oils and fats in 1996/97, but prices will dictate production and sales, a U.N. official said on Thursday.

Global production of edible/soap fats and oils is expected to rise 1.5 percent to 97 million tonnes in 1996/97, M. Maftei, a commodities specialist with the United Nations, told the Vegoils, Oilseeds and Meals '97 conference in Kuala Lumpur.

"Domestic production of oils in the largest importing countries is unlikely to be sufficient to meet their consumption needs and stocks will probably have to be drawn down to below normal levels by the end of the season," Maftei said at the conference, organised by the Singapore-based Centre for Management Technology.
However she cautioned that the growth will be rationed by the relatively high prices of fats and oils products.
Maftei said world production of the seven major oilseeds in 1996/97 is estimated at 263 million tonnes, one percent higher than in 1995/96.
Soybean is expected to lead the field with 133.4 million tonnes, up seven percent from last season's production, Maftei said.

She said Brazil, one of the largest growers of soybeans, is expected to produce 26 million tonnes in the current season, up three million tonnes from previously, due to favourable prices and improved credit facilities for farms.

Maftei did not forecast production in United States, the world's largest soybean grower and exporter. But she said U.S. farmers were expected to use the country's new "freedom to farm" law to plant up to 27.8 million hectares of soybeans in 1996/97, up 7.0 percent from the previous season.
A deficit in soybean production is, however, expected in China, where imports of the material are estimated to be two to three times higher than previously, Maftei said.
She said China's import of oils and fats is seen rising 25 percent to 3.8 million tonnes in 1996/97 due to lower domestic oilseeds output.
World production of rapeseed in the current season is estimated at 30.2 million tonnes and cottonseed at 34.3 million tonnes, Maftei said. --Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-2307509)
